study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are clearly stated: the study applies normative modeling to map inter-individual differences in ADHD and to examine how case–control analyses may conceal individual-level heterogeneity. This directly addresses purpose and research questions.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Methods. Using a normative modeling approach, we mapped inter-individual differences... to examine the degree to which case-control analyses disguise differences between individuals.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Eligibility criteria for healthy individuals are described (no current neurological or mental disorder per DIVA/SCID, no first-degree relatives with ADHD/major disorders). Final sample size for controls is reported (N=146). However, explicit image quality control standards and detailed exclusion reasons are not described.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Additional inclusion criteria for healthy individuals were: (viii) no current neurological or mental disorder according to DIVA, SCID-I, or SCID-II ... (ix) no first-degree relatives with ADHD or other major mental disorders. ... Total (N) | Healthy individuals 146

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled as covariates in the normative model. Data are single-site; therefore, no site-effect handling is required.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: we estimated normative brain changes ... using Gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The healthy reference cohort appears to be locally collected at Radboud University Medical Center and matched to ADHD participants. The collection site is clear, but the time period is not specified.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Participants with persistent ADHD were recruited from the Department of Psychiatry of the Radboud University Medical Center and through advertisements... matched ... to a healthy individual population. All participants were Dutch and of European Caucasian ancestry.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Primary data collection with modality, acquisition parameters, and equipment specified: 1.5T Siemens Avanto, MPRAGE, TR/TE/TI, flip angle, FOV, voxel size, and head coil are reported.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Whole brain imaging was performed using a 1.5 T scanner (Magnetom Avanto, Siemens Medical Systems) ... MPRAGE ... TR 2730 ms, TE 2.95 ms, TI 1000 ms, flip angle 7°, FOV 256×256×176 mm3, voxel size 1.0×1.0×1.0 mm3.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described (SPM12 new segment, DARTEL normalization, 8-mm FWHM smoothing). However, explicit quality control procedures are not detailed.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: T1 images were rigidly aligned using SPM-12 ... segmented, normalized, and bias field-corrected using 'new segment' ... DARTEL ... Subsequently, all gray matter volumes were smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Internal validation via 10-fold cross-validation is used on healthy individuals when estimating the normative range.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The normative range for this model in healthy individuals was estimated using 10-fold crossvalidation...

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset is used for validation; the model is trained on local healthy controls with cross-validation and then applied to ADHD participants.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: ... estimated using 10-fold crossvalidation, then we applied the model trained on all healthy individuals to participants with ADHD.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical model is specified as Gaussian process regression with age and sex covariates; downstream analyses include PALM with FDR/TFCE. Software environment (Python 3.6) and SPM12 are given. However, specific GPR library and kernel settings are not detailed.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: normative models were estimated using Gaussian process regression (Rasmussen and Williams, 2006)... we computed a Z-score for each voxel ... We estimated mean group-level deviations ... using PALM ... All analyses were performed in python3.6.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative model fit metrics for the reference cohort (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, calibration coverage). The focus is on deviation maps and group contrasts/overlaps.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: [No explicit metrics such as R2/MAE/coverage reported; methods describe CV and deviation computation without reporting fit statistics.]

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation is used, sample sizes and demographics for each partition (train/validation/test) are not reported.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: The normative range ... estimated using 10-fold crossvalidation... [no per-partition characteristics described]

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software environment and tools are partially specified (SPM-12, PALM, Python 3.6). Availability of code, trained models, or data is not stated; specific library versions for GPR are not provided.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: All analyses were performed in python3.6 ... SPM-12 ... PALM (Winkler et al., 2015).

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Patient eligibility and diagnostic criteria are clearly described (DIVA confirming DSM-IV-TR ADHD persistence; SCID-I/II; IQ>70; exclusions). Final sample size is reported (N=153). Image quality/data completeness standards and explicit exclusion reasons are not detailed.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: The diagnostic interview for persistent ADHD (DIVA) was conducted to confirm the diagnosis ... SCID-I and SCID-II ... inclusion criteria ... (i) DSM-IV-TR criteria ... (v) no neurological disorders ... Total (N) ... ADHD 153

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses consider clinical covariates including symptom scores, comorbidity, and stimulant medication in relation to deviation scores (per supplement).
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Supplemental Table 1: Association of deviations from the normative model with age, comorbidity, stimulant medication, and symptom scores in ADHD ... we tested for associations between the percentage of extremely deviating voxels and age, symptom scores, and comorbidity.

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort data source is described as recruitment from Radboud University Medical Center and advertisements, but the collection time period is not specified.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Participants with persistent ADHD were recruited from the Department of Psychiatry of the Radboud University Medical Center and through advertisements.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample size, demographics (age, sex), and clinical characteristics (symptom scores, comorbidity, medication status) are reported in Table 1.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Table 1. Demographics and clinical characteristics ... Total (N) ... ADHD 153 ... Males (%) 41.2% ... Age (years) 35.05 ± 10.81 ... Hyperactivity/impulsivity ... Inattention ... Comorbidities ... Stimulant medication Current/Past/No.

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical measures and assessment procedures are described: DIVA structured interview for ADHD diagnosis; ADHD Rating Scale-IV; SCID-I/II for comorbidities.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: The diagnostic interview for persistent ADHD (DIVA) ... The ADHD Rating Scale-IV was filled in by each participant ... To assess comorbidities, the structured clinical interviews (SCID-I and SCID-II) for DSM-IV were administered.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are explicitly defined as voxelwise Z-scores (predicted vs. true normalized by uncertainty); thresholds (|Z|>2.6) are reported; clinical significance is explored through associations with diagnosis, symptoms, age, and comorbidity and discussion of heterogeneity.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: ... computing a Z-score for each voxel, reflecting the difference between the predicted volume and the true volume normalized by the uncertainty ... maps were thresholded at |Z| > 2.6 ... We tested for associations between diagnosis and those scores ... and ... between the percentage of extremely deviating voxels and age, symptom scores, and comorbidity.
